skill.name: artifacts
skill.description: Build, debug, or review code that uses Cloudflare Artifacts, Git-compatible versioned storage, from Workers, the REST API, or Git clients. Use for the env.ARTIFACTS binding, creating, forking, or importing repositories, repo-scoped tokens, and pushing commits from a Worker.
skill.summary: Build and troubleshoot Git-backed storage workflows with Cloudflare Artifacts, Workers, and Wrangler.
skill.author: cloudflare

security_audit.summary: Twenty-five flags are false positives: documentation links, Markdown formatting, or benign feedback text. The Wrangler command can download and execute a package when no local copy is installed. The verification steps also advise deleting repositories or tokens without explicitly restricting cleanup to disposable local resources.

remediation.suggestion: Use the Wrangler version pinned in the project lockfile and invoke the installed binary. Require approval before installing or updating Wrangler.
Test in a fresh local simulator namespace. Limit cleanup to resources created for the current test, and require explicit approval before deleting or revoking deployed resources.

semantic_findings.description: The verification section tells agents to delete repositories or tokens they created while exploring. It does not limit deletion to the simulator or require approval for deployed resources. Following it remotely could remove repository data or revoke access.

content.value_statement: Cloudflare Artifacts splits repository management and Git writes across different interfaces. This skill helps you choose the right interface and verify your code against current documentation and generated types.
actual_capabilities: Find the documentation for Workers bindings, REST endpoints, Wrangler commands, and Git operations.
Check binding methods, return types, and errors against the Wrangler-generated TypeScript declarations.
Plan repository creation, forking, and imports, including how to handle an import that is still running.
Design Worker commits and pushes with a Git client and short-lived repository write tokens.
Plan local verification for an empty namespace, a Worker restart, and concurrent pushes.
limitations: The skill contains guidance and links, not a bundled utility or test suite.
Exact API signatures depend on the installed Wrangler version and the available documentation.
The Workers binding manages repositories but cannot commit file changes without a Git client.
Local simulator tests do not verify permissions or repository state in a deployed environment.

use_cases.title: Save versioned files from a Worker
use_cases.description: Plan how a Worker creates a repository, makes its first commit, and pushes with a short-lived write token.

use_cases.title: Plan a repository migration
use_cases.description: Choose the REST API or Wrangler for imports and determine how to handle repositories that are still importing.

use_cases.title: Review repository credential handling
use_cases.description: Check token scope, lifetime, storage, and use at the approved Git remote.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how Artifacts namespaces, repositories, and Git remotes relate. Tell me when to use the Workers binding, REST API, or a Git client.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Worker binding
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Artifacts binding configuration and generated Wrangler types. Identify incorrect method names or return types without making remote changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the first Git push
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: add file writes to a Worker
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan how my Worker can create a repository if needed and push the first commit with a short-lived write token. Include an isolated local test.

prompt_templates.title: Review concurrent writes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Worker for repository creation races, pending imports, rejected pushes, and stale tokens. Propose bounded retries and tests that do not modify deployed repositories.

output_examples.input: Why does my Worker fail when it tries to clone a newly created repository?
output_examples.output: A new repository has no commits to clone. Initialize a working tree, create the first commit, and push it using a Git client.

output_examples.input: Two requests tried to create the same repository. How should I handle the second request?
output_examples.output: If creation returns ALREADY_EXISTS, another request may have created it first. Look up the repository again and handle any other error by its code.

output_examples.input: What should the Worker do if another writer pushes first?
output_examples.output: Fetch the updated branch, reapply your change, and retry within a fixed limit. Do not force-push over the other writer.

best_practices: Check the current documentation and generated binding types before using a method.
Mint a short-lived write token for the intended repository and keep it out of logs.
Test first-run behavior in a fresh local simulator namespace, then restart the Worker and repeat the checks.
anti_patterns: Expecting the Workers binding to write files or create Git commits.
Matching error message text instead of using stable error codes.
Reusing the initial repository token from module scope for later pushes.

faq.question: What is Cloudflare Artifacts?
faq.answer: It is Git-compatible versioned storage. Namespaces contain repositories, and each repository has a Git remote.

faq.question: Can the Workers binding write files?
faq.answer: No. Use a Git client to commit changes and push them to the repository remote.

faq.question: Where can I find the correct binding signatures?
faq.answer: Check the TypeScript declarations generated by the Wrangler version installed in your project. Use the binding reference for additional context.

faq.question: How should I handle a missing repository?
faq.answer: Check the error code before creating anything. If another request creates the repository first, look it up again.

faq.question: Should I reuse the token returned when I create a repository?
faq.answer: Prefer a fresh, short-lived token with write scope when you need to push. Do not store it in module scope.

faq.question: Can I test this without touching deployed repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Use an isolated local simulator namespace and verify that your Wrangler configuration does not target remote resources.
